author_reading_scope: Inspected the full-text Bar-Natan–Stoimenow PDF (30 PDF pages) and read §1.1, PDF pp. 3–5, in full. Inspected the complete 509-page Chmutov–Duzhin–Mostovoy book and read §§3.1.1, 3.4, 3.5.1, 4.1, 4.2.1–4.2.2, plus §2.2.1 and §3.2.2. These passages cover singular derivatives, chord diagrams, framed zero markers, 4T/1T, the framed distinction, the mixed-crossing linking formula, and the type-one link example. The Kontsevich integration proof is a KT-35 boundary; its rational theorem is used only as external input for the scalar-extension remark, not as a premise in the KT-34 symbol, 4T, or 1T claims. Chmutov–Lando (2007), §2, PDF pp. 2–3, supports the rational unframed theorem; the scalar-extension steps are proved locally by finite-dimensional linear algebra.

author_read_locators.disposition: Framing-zero dots are used only as auxiliary singularity bookkeeping; framed weight-system modules here are generated by ordinary chord diagrams modulo 4T.

author_read_locators.locator: §§4.2.1–4.2.2, printed pp. 92–94: necessity of 1T/4T for unframed symbols, the integration theorem statement, and framed 4T/no-1T distinction.
author_read_locators.disposition: The necessary direction and framed distinction are incorporated locally. The book states the integration theorem for R=C; the separate unframed rational theorem is supported by Chmutov–Lando (2007), and the remark proves extension to every characteristic-zero field by finite-dimensional scalar extension. The integration theorem remains a KT-35 boundary and is not used as a premise.

author_read_locators.disposition: Used for the explicit local crossing arithmetic; the item independently computes first and second finite differences.
